key_insight: Solver-independent certificates provide guaranteed error bounds for PDE outputs, exposing errors that convergence studies can miss.
engineering_relevance: An independent checker can verify third-party, LLM-written, and neural solver outputs against specified physics without trusting their implementations.
method: Return an admissible potential and an exactly charge-conserving current as a certificate.
Use a small independent checker to compute guaranteed error bounds.
Apply the same checker to finite-element solvers and neural predictions.
evidence_signal: The checker rejected or refuted all five bugs that passed grid-convergence tests, certified one LLM-written solver to 0.1%, and bounded reduced-basis neural predictions with intervals at most 0.0021% wide in-range.
watch_item: Bounds apply to the stated model, not physical reality, and become informative only with energy-accurate outputs on a sufficiently resolving grid.
paper_title: Verifying the Outputs of PDE Solvers: From Finite Elements to Neural Surrogates
